title: Save your training infobase and verify a separate copy
goal: Dump your training infobase and verify a separate restoration while preserving original work.
prerequisites: Your own training infobase; be able to close and reopen its modes one at a time.
Know how to create a separate folder for a backup.
outcomes: Save .dt and distinguish it from a .cf definition.
Identify a new empty target by entry and directory.
Restore a copy and state what was actually compared.
sections: A learning infobase needs its own directory and a clear name. Do not select an arbitrary infobase from a shared list. Before creating it, verify that the target directory is new and the source work remains intact. Never restore over an existing infobase. Isolation protects working data from learning mistakes and makes the experiment repeatable.

Use the platform startup window to add a new infobase without a configuration. Empty state is expected in A1. The supplied native probe instead creates a separate workspace, loads original Nexus metadata and executes BSL. Creating an infobase alone does not establish that a complete service application exists.

A learner has at least two different results: configuration and records in installed 1C, plus completion marks and notes in Nexus. Backing up one does not transfer the other. An infobase dump file, .dt, restores the 1C infobase; it is not a certificate and contains no Nexus course progress. Saving source in Studio is not a complete infobase backup either.

Configuration sources describe structure and code. They do not back up particular customers or documents. An infobase dump transfers its state, but usefulness is established by restoring elsewhere and inspecting the result. A file with the expected extension is weak evidence by itself.

Copying an active file infobase can capture inconsistent state. Close sessions first and follow the official dump/restore workflow. Do not keep Designer and a training-edition user session open together because the edition allows only one session. Preserve earlier attempts: a new test should not destroy evidence of the previous failure.

Give each dump a new descriptive name with a date or purpose. For example, Before_change_01.dt and After_check_02.dt are different files. A file’s existence does not prove that it can be restored. Test it by loading a specifically created empty infobase and comparing expected objects and records. The original remains unchanged during this experiment.

Moving from A to P creates new work with a new ID and source provenance. Content may be copied, but completion, test results and assessment from the source trajectory are not awarded. The candidate applies this mechanism only to local learning notes; an actual infobase must be copied separately with official tools.

Record source course, target course, new ID, date and synthetic-data status. Edit the new note and reopen the source. If the original text also changes, you have shared a reference or overwritten it rather than making an independent copy. The software model needs a deep copy; infobase work needs a separate restore destination.

A .cf configuration file and a .dt infobase dump serve different purposes. Type definitions without user records do not replace a data backup. Use the infobase dump command in Designer’s Administration menu for this lesson. Our empty infobase has no customer records yet: expect to restore an empty training application, not to acquire completed course examples.

A1 acceptance includes explaining layers, modes and objects, a navigation protocol, a separate infobase and evidence that the source survives. Nexus completion is learner self-report, not a protected exam. Author automation demonstrates a particular probe on a specified version, not a learner’s personal performance.

Without the official platform, theory, diagrams, questions and notes remain available offline. Leave the native lab unattested. You may enter P1 directly: A is not a mandatory prerequisite for P. Before continuing, preserve the environment record, control results and explicitly untested items.

Finish by reopening the original and checking that you did not accidentally continue work in the copy. Give the copy its own visible startup name. For later experiments, record which work it came from and why it was created. A short human-readable note is enough; a complex JSON protocol is not a beginner prerequisite. Keep a failed attempt alongside its correction when it explains your conclusion.

lab.title: .dt dump and restoration into a new infobase
lab.environment: Your own file infobase in the official installed training platform; a new empty target for the check.
steps: Close your own application sessions. Save intended configuration edits and update the database configuration normally. In the startup list select the original training entry and verify its directory before opening Designer. The Designer title can display the configuration name rather than the startup entry name.
Choose a new directory for your training backups. Give the .dt file a new name, such as Service_desk_before_01.dt. Confirm and wait for the normal completion message.

Close the source Designer. Create an infobase without a configuration in a new empty folder and name its startup entry “Service desk — restore check”. Select that new entry, verify its directory beneath the list, then open Designer from that entry.

Confirm that this Designer was launched from the new empty target entry whose directory you checked. If unsure, cancel and return to the startup list; a matching window title is insufficient. Choose Administration → Load infobase and select your .dt. Read the replacement warning and continue only for the new empty target. Wait for completion and the normal restart if prompted.

Close the restoration target. Open the original and restored infobases in Enterprise mode, one at a time. Compare expected objects and records. Both empty infobases normally have no application sections. Record source, copy name and observation in Nexus.
expected: The intended source is selected and no other session of your own remains open.
A separate .dt file exists and the operation has finished.
A second entry has another name and directory; its Designer is open.
The new infobase opens after loading and shows the saved training state.
Both infobases remain independently available; the original is intact and the copy matches the dump state.
evidence: A new .dt filename and the standard dump completion result.
Different source and target names and directories, free of third-party data.
Reopening and comparison results, plus recognition that .dt does not restore Nexus progress.
lab.negative: Before loading, check which startup entry and directory you selected. If the target is uncertain, cancel and return to the list. Source and copy can share the same window title. A destructive load is not needed to test this mistake.

mistakes: Check the task and command name. Saving the configuration definition does not promise preservation of customer records.
A file exists, so the backup must work.
Restore into a new empty target and check the expected state.
I am restoring into completed work.
Stop before confirmation. This lab uses a new empty target.
Nexus progress did not return after loading .dt.
It uses separate storage. A 1C dump transfers neither your Nexus account nor course completion marks.

quiz.question: Where should you restore a learning dump?
quiz.explanation: Verify restoration without overwriting the source.

quiz.question: What transfers from A to P?
options: New copied work content and provenance

quiz.question: What is strong backup verification?
quiz.explanation: You must demonstrate recovery of the original state.

review: Separate platform observations from model results.

examples.expected: Two infobases appear in the startup list; the original keeps its state.
examples.explanation: Restoration targets a new location. The dump links it to its source, while a clear startup-entry name and verified directory identify the correct target before launch.
trace: Check its contents, then compare the original.

examples.title: Why .cf is insufficient
examples.source: Only a .cf configuration file exists; entered customer records must be restored.
examples.expected: Do not promise customer-record recovery from .cf alone.
examples.explanation: Configuration defines structure. Restoring the entire infobase requires an appropriate data backup, such as a standard .dt dump.

route.program: Installed 1C Designer; Windows File Explorer for choosing the backup file

steps.title: Finish working in the original
steps.action: Close your own application sessions. Save intended configuration edits and update the database configuration normally. In the startup list select the original training entry and verify its directory before opening Designer. The Designer title can display the configuration name rather than the startup entry name.
steps.why: Back up an identifiable saved state rather than unsaved editor text.
steps.expected: The intended source is selected and no other session of your own remains open.
steps.troubleshooting: Save unsaved code separately and resolve the update first. Do not dump a similarly named infobase at random.
steps.before: Use only your own training infobase. Its application sessions are closed and no edits are unsaved.

steps.title: Dump the infobase
steps.action: Choose a new directory for your training backups. Give the .dt file a new name, such as Service_desk_before_01.dt. Confirm and wait for the normal completion message.
steps.why: This command saves the infobase rather than only its configuration definition.
steps.expected: A separate .dt file exists and the operation has finished.
steps.troubleshooting: Do not substitute Save configuration to file. If the name exists, choose another to retain the previous backup.
steps.before: The intended source is selected and no other session of your own remains open.

steps.title: Create an empty restoration target
steps.action: Close the source Designer. Create an infobase without a configuration in a new empty folder and name its startup entry “Service desk — restore check”. Select that new entry, verify its directory beneath the list, then open Designer from that entry.
steps.why: Loading replaces the selected target’s content; a new empty target preserves existing work.
steps.expected: A second entry has another name and directory; its Designer is open.
steps.troubleshooting: If unsure which target you launched, close your own Designer and verify the entry and directory in the startup list again. The source and copy can have identical window titles.
steps.before: A separate .dt file exists and the operation has finished.

steps.title: Load only the new target
steps.where: New target’s Designer → Administration → Load infobase
steps.action: Confirm that this Designer was launched from the new empty target entry whose directory you checked. If unsure, cancel and return to the startup list; a matching window title is insufficient. Choose Administration → Load infobase and select your .dt. Read the replacement warning and continue only for the new empty target. Wait for completion and the normal restart if prompted.
steps.why: Test whether the dump can actually be restored. The original is not the target.
steps.expected: The new infobase opens after loading and shows the saved training state.
steps.troubleshooting: Retain an unreadable dump and the error separately. Do not troubleshoot by loading over the original.
steps.before: A second entry has another name and directory; its Designer is open.

steps.title: Reopen both infobases
steps.action: Close the restoration target. Open the original and restored infobases in Enterprise mode, one at a time. Compare expected objects and records. Both empty infobases normally have no application sections. Record source, copy name and observation in Nexus.
steps.why: Actual reopening supplements the file and success message.
steps.expected: Both infobases remain independently available; the original is intact and the copy matches the dump state.
steps.troubleshooting: If records differ, check dump time and the selected file. Do not change source data just to obtain matching screenshots.
steps.before: The new infobase opens after loading and shows the saved training state.
